q: Can you provide SEO services remotely?
a: Yes. Audits, keyword research, content plans and implementation reviews can be managed remotely with access to the site, Search Console and analytics.

q: What is the difference between local and international SEO?
a: Local SEO focuses on nearby searches, Business Profiles, reviews and relevant service areas. International SEO handles language, country targeting, site structure and market-specific content.

q: Do I need a page for every city I serve?
a: Only where you can offer distinct, useful information about that service area. Near-duplicate city pages with swapped place names are weak for visitors and search engines.

q: Can a business rank in a city without an office there?
a: Organic pages may rank when they genuinely serve the market. Google Maps visibility is strongly affected by proximity and eligibility; do not create a fake address or Business Profile.

q: How do you research local SEO keywords?
a: Look at service terms, neighbourhood language, map results and questions from actual customers. Search demand and competition can change substantially across nearby cities.

q: Does Google Business Profile replace a website?
a: No. A Business Profile supports local discovery, while a useful website explains services, builds trust and gives customers a clear way to enquire or buy.

q: How long does local SEO take?
a: Basic accuracy fixes may be reflected sooner, but building useful location pages, reviews and local authority takes sustained work. The market and starting position affect timing.

q: What do you report for location SEO?
a: Measure relevant local queries, organic and map visibility where available, and calls or enquiries from the target market. Compare against a clear baseline and period.
